instruction:
Read the Rust Book sections What Is Ownership?, References and Borrowing, and The Slice Type. Build a three-part explanation for a new Rust programmer. First compare assigning a String to a second variable with explicitly cloning it, stating which original variable remains usable and why. Second state the documented rules for simultaneous mutable and immutable references and explain when a reference stops being used in the example with two printed references followed by a mutable reference. Third compare returning a numeric first-word index with returning a string slice, and explain how the slice version prevents the documented clear-the-string mistake. Include one relevant listing number or section heading per part and a URL for each of the three sections. Describe the book examples without executing or compiling any code.

Stopping condition: Stop when all three explanations are complete, identify their supporting examples or headings, and cite the three distinct Rust Book sections.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Part 1: What Is Ownership? (String assignment vs cloning)
items.description: Provide the explanation comparing assigning a String to a second variable versus explicitly cloning it, including stating which original variable remains usable and explaining why (e.g., move semantics vs deep copy). Full credit if both the comparison and the usability explanation are accurate based on the text.

items.criterion: Part 2: References and Borrowing (Simultaneous references and scope)
items.description: State the documented rules for simultaneous mutable and immutable references, and explain when a reference stops being used, specifically referencing the example with two printed references followed by a mutable reference. Full credit if the rules and the explanation of reference scope (Non-Lexical Lifetimes) are accurate based on the text.

items.criterion: Part 3: The Slice Type (Numeric index vs string slice)
items.description: Compare returning a numeric first-word index with returning a string slice, and explain how the slice version prevents the documented clear-the-string mistake. Full credit if the comparison and the explanation of how slices tie the borrow to the original string are accurate based on the text.

Include a relevant URL for each of the three distinct Rust Book sections (What Is Ownership, References and Borrowing, The Slice Type), and include one relevant listing number or section heading for each of the three parts. Full credit if all 3 URLs and 3 headings/listings are provided correctly.
Describe the book examples based purely on the text without attempting to execute or compile any code. Full credit if no code execution tools (like Python or bash to run rustc) were used.
